claim: 'Screw that cylinder': instead of committing to a fixed segment count on a Cylinder primitive up front, build only a flat half-profile (a strip of edges tracing the desired cross-section, centered on the object's own origin), then add a Screw modifier to revolve that profile into a full cylindrical/lathe shape. The segment count becomes a live modifier parameter that can be changed at any time -- even after later modifiers like Boolean are stacked on top -- instead of being locked in at mesh-creation time and forcing a full restart if it turns out wrong.
supporting_evidence: Direct quotes (~34:45 onward): "this is where screw that cylinder comes into place... we're going to start with shape or another primitive that actually doesn't resemble a cylinder at all but with the help of a Nifty little modifier and blender we're going to create a awesome Dynamic cylinder that we're able to update those divisions after its creation... in object mode I'm going to select my profile here I'll go to modifier and I'll type in screw and now from that profile we have created a perfect cylinder the beauty about this is that we could actually dynamically change the divisions here"; stated problem it solves: "the ability to change primitive divisions after they have been created it's not one of them [Blender's strong points]... nine times out of 10 you'll have to restart your shape"
rejected_alternative: Building a standard Cylinder primitive with a fixed vertex count chosen up front, then discovering mid-build that the count was wrong and needing to restart or awkwardly hand-subdivide
reason: A baked-in primitive segment count can't be changed non-destructively once other modeling (booleans, etc.) is stacked on top; a Screw-modifier cylinder keeps the segment count as a live, adjustable parameter for the entire build.

transfer_tests.expected_effect: segment count changeable after mesh creation via a live Screw-modifier parameter, without rebuilding the base mesh
transfer_tests.observed_effect: base mesh stayed at 5 vertices throughout; changing the Screw modifier's steps from 8 to 16 changed the evaluated mesh from 40 to 80 vertices (32 to 64 faces) with 0 degenerate faces and 0 pinch candidates at both settings -- core claim confirmed. NOT tested: the claim's stronger form (segment count stays adjustable even after later modifiers like Boolean are stacked on top) -- this run only tested the Screw modifier in isolation. See runs/2026-08-14_transfer-test-screw-cylinder/brief.md.

claim: 'Pattern match merge': to merge a small, dense, highly-detailed part onto a larger, sparser part in a SubD workflow, first Shrinkwrap the detail's base onto the target surface so it already conforms before any pattern is even modeled on it, build the repeating pattern (e.g. via an Array modifier) so it's easy to adjust, then before joining the two objects, select and reinforce the edges of the *sparser* target mesh that will receive the detail with a full Edge Crease (mean crease = 1) and add a Subdivision Surface modifier baked into that base mesh to raise its local vertex density closer to the detailed part's density -- only then join the objects and manually weld/clean up the remaining vertex mismatches.
supporting_evidence: Direct quotes (~16:40-18:14): "the first thing that you'll see me do even before I get to the nitty-gritty of creating that initial detail is I'm actually shrink wrapping this via shrink wrap modifier this little bit of a base onto the main shape that it's going to be merged to... we're trying to match up the two densities... the key here is that we're going to have to actually reinforce some of these edges first select all the edges that need to be hardened or reinforced and set those edges to a mean crease of one that's going to allow us to hold up our shape once we introduce our added divisions so on this base mesh we could add a subdivision modifier and actually bake it in"

claim: For a shape with N-fold radial symmetry (car rim, gun part, anything repeating around a circle): (1) count the real number of repeats to get the symmetry order N, (2) start with a primitive whose vertex/segment count divides evenly by N, (3) model only one slice, then cut that slice in half again and use a Mirror modifier so only a quarter (half of one slice) needs to be hand-modeled, (4) compute the per-repeat rotation as 360/N, (5) set up an Empty at the object's origin and drive an Array modifier's Object Offset off that Empty with the computed Y rotation set on the Empty, count = N -- apply all transforms on both the slice and the Empty first or the array output is garbled.
supporting_evidence: Direct quotes (~11:55-14:10): "I want to start with A Primitive that's evenly divisible by six... 60 divided by 6 that gives us 10 faces per slice... we only need to select five as we're only going to be working on half of that one slice with that... we'll drop a mirror modifier... 360 divided by your symmetry lines which is six it's going to give us 60 so this slice is going to have to be rotated 60 degrees... we'll use a object offset here we'll pick this empty here and you see that it's off in la la land well why is that well that's cuz of our transforms again so what we'll do is we'll hit control a we'll apply all our transforms"
rejected_alternative: Manually modeling and duplicating each of the N repeats by hand
reason: Modeling only a quarter-slice and driving the rest procedurally via mirror + empty-driven array means every edit only has to be made once and propagates automatically to the full radial pattern.

claim: A Bevel that produces visibly wrong/wonky results even though the underlying edge selection and geometry look correct is very often caused by flipped face normals on the affected faces, not a geometry problem -- check the 'Face Orientation' viewport overlay first (flipped faces render in a different highlight color), select just the flipped faces, and use Mesh > Normals > Flip before troubleshooting the bevel any further.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (~40:00-40:13): "something that you want to make sure to check into for example if I want to Bevel this Edge and you're getting wonkiness uh the geometry is actually fine it's an issue with the face normals so to identify that you go to your viewport overlays here face orientation and you see that this is flip... we go to mesh normals flip now these are flipped"

claim: To make several duplicated/instanced copies of a detail (e.g. repeated belt loops posed differently around a character) stay updatable from one master edit: build and clean the master copy at the world origin with transforms applied, create the other copies with Alt+D (linked duplicate -- shares mesh data so edit-mode edits to the master propagate to every copy automatically), then pose/rotate/scale each *copy* only at the object level (object-level transforms are independent per-instance; edit-mode mesh edits are shared). For modifiers (which don't propagate to linked duplicates by default): select all copies then the master, Ctrl+L > Copy Modifiers to give every copy the same modifier stack, then on each modifier's driven parameter (e.g. Solidify thickness) right-click the master's field > Copy as New Driver, and right-click the same field on each copy > Paste Driver, so adjusting the master's modifier settings live-updates every copy.
supporting_evidence: Direct quotes (~8:38-8:48, plus earlier setup): "I'll go here to the thickness on my control copy I'll right click and I will do copy as new driver now I'll go to each one of these instances and in the thickness I'll right click and I'll do paste driver you'll see this purple color coding indicating that this connection is now alive"; and: "by default the modifiers are not passed down to the instances so we'll have to actually link them with a two-step process... I'll select all my instances select the modifier that we're basically sourcing I'll do control L... copy modifiers"
rejected_alternative: Manually re-modeling or re-applying every change to each duplicated instance separately
reason: Linked duplicates (Alt+D) already share mesh-edit changes automatically; drivers extend that same live-update behavior to modifier parameters, which linked duplication alone doesn't cover.
